newsitem.title: USA: Centurion BHP find Utah copper.
newsitem.headline: Centurion BHP find Utah copper.

text.p: Centurion Mines Corp said Wednesday BHP Mineral International Exploration Inc believes it has found a large porphyry copper deposit on the "Little Bingham" Copper/Gold Mining Property.
The "Little Bingham" property is located in the West Tintic Mining District, about 70 miles southwest of Salt Lake City and 14 miles west of Eureka, Utah.
Centurion said the Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd subsidiary has drilled three holes totaling 3,190 feet on the property.

BHP's drill hole No. 96-3 showed the presence of quartz monzonite host rocks containing various sulphide minerals with elevated copper and molybdenum values, Centurion said, adding this geological environment is suggestive of an extensive porphyry system.
It said BHP is planning additional exploration drilling during 1997 to further explore the porphyry target area.

Due to the "favorable exploration results," a Centurion official said, the 12,000 acres covered by the company's joint venture with BHP, formed a year ago, "has been significantly expanded by 1,340 additional acres of mining claims and mineral leases."

Under the terms of the joint venture, BHP has the option to earn up to 75 percent interest in the project by paying all costs through a positive feasibility study, with periodic cash payments to Centurion.

After earn-in, Centurion said, it can maintain a working interest by paying 25 percent of costs, or may convert to a 15 percent net profits royalty interest with all costs being paid by BHP. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
